category_info.ripening_signs: Uniform red to deep dark burgundy coloration, firm yet slight give, sweet aroma, and easy detachment with stem attached
category_info.pollination: Depends on variety; sour cherries are usually self-fertile, whereas many sweet cherries require a cross-pollination partner
category_info.pruning_season: Late spring to mid-summer (dry conditions) to minimize fungal and bacterial canker infection risks
category_info.watering_need: Deep watering every 7-10 days during dry spells; approximately 2.5 cm per week
category_info.sunlight_need: Full sun (at least 6-8 hours of direct sunlight daily)

observations.symptom: Uniform green foliage with intact serrated margins
observations.evidence: Leaf shows normal ovate shape, serrate margins, and deep green pigmentation without signs of chlorosis or necrosis.
Micro-reflections across the cuticle consistent with camera flash glare on epidermal cells, with no distinct chlorotic feeding halos.

possible_causes.name: Healthy leaf tissue
possible_causes.reason: The leaf shows well-developed cellular structure, clear venation, intact margin teeth, and uniform green color indicative of good vigor.

possible_causes.name: Early mite feeding stippling
possible_causes.reason: Tiny light dots across the blade could mimic early-stage two-spotted spider mite feeding, though they appear to be lighting artifacts from flash photography.

recommended_actions.action: Maintain routine cultural care without pesticide applications
recommended_actions.reason: The foliage displays no actionable disease or pest damage; preventive care and proper hydration are sufficient.

recommended_actions.action: Inspect the undersides of leaves in daylight with a hand lens
recommended_actions.reason: Rules out any presence of microscopic mites or early fungal spores that cannot be confirmed from a single detached leaf photo.

seasonal_context: During active spring and summer growth, ensure consistent soil moisture and adequate air circulation in the canopy to prevent fungal pathogens.
what_to_monitor: Appearance of circular purple-brown spots or shot-holes characteristic of cherry leaf spot
White powdery patches on newly expanding terminal foliage
Fine webbing or bronze discoloration on leaf surfaces
limitations: Only a single detached leaf is visible against an artificial background; whole-plant architecture, stem condition, and overall orchard health cannot be assessed.
Specular flash reflection makes it difficult to definitively differentiate between natural cuticle shine and very subtle early pest stippling.
follow_up_questions: Are there any other leaves on the tree showing spotting, yellowing, or leaf drop?
Do you see any fine webbing or moving specks on the underside of similar leaves?
